init_caller_authorized.meaning: Whether the address invoking BuilderWallet.init is authorized (the legitimate builder or its designated admin) to set builderAdmin.
init_caller_authorized.checkpoint: at init invocation, before builderAdmin is written
init_caller_authorized.evidence: since there is no guards on `BuilderWallet.init`, anyone can call it and overwrite the `builderAdmin` address, which is used to guard `sweep` from being called by anyone. In practice, any builder fees accumulated in these wallets can be stolen because of that.

admin_overwritten.meaning: Whether BuilderWallet.builderAdmin was overwritten with an attacker-controlled address by an init call.
admin_overwritten.evidence: since there is no guards on `BuilderWallet.init`, anyone can call it and overwrite the `builderAdmin` address, which is used to guard `sweep` from being called by anyone. In practice, any builder fees accumulated in these wallets can be stolen because of that.

effect_coverage.reason: Program-generated exact coverage for selected direct impact.

assumptions: The legitimate builder (or deployer) is the intended initial builderAdmin and sole authorized init caller (a_legit_admin_assumption); the attacker is not that authorized caller.
The unauthorized init invocation completes successfully and overwrites builderAdmin on the deployed builder wallet contract (i_admin_overwritten).
builderAdmin is the sole guard for sweep, so an attacker who becomes builderAdmin controls sweep (p_admin_guards_sweep, s_intent).

limitations: i_fees_stolen (fee theft via sweep) is deferred as a secondary consequence: it additionally requires accumulated fees (p_fees_accumulated) and a subsequent successful sweep call by the new builderAdmin; the report describes it as potential, not an observed incident.
The concrete authorized init caller address is undefined; authorization is modeled relationally via init_caller_authorized.
Only sweep is cited as guarded by builderAdmin; the effect of the admin overwrite on any other guarded functions is not bound.
Whether init is one-time-only is unstated; the binding covers any unauthorized init invocation.
